title: A Brave Pawn Runs
reviewNotes: All 34 saved states and captions reviewed; native images 25, 27 and 32 establish two complete later positions. Four selected branches check the six-piece h-pawn race after Kb6 at 79s and the separate seven-piece b6 pawn mate after Bxa6 at 109s. The source larger setup is outside exact verification. Immediate h7 wins while independent Kxd7/Be4/h7/Bxh7 draws. Representative ...Be6 cannot prevent h8=Q. The two source variations are explicitly separate, not joined through unseen moves.

So actually the first move that needs to be found here is to sacrifice the pawn by promoting it to either a queen or a rook. doesn't really change because in either situation the queen is forced to capture the new piece and now we can follow up with rook to B6 check. Of course, the only move is for the king to come up. White is actually preparing checkmate net with B5 and there is no way to stop this checkmate. The rook is simply coming to A6. Believe it or not, what the engine wants in this position is to sacrifice the queen to get the rook. But now in this position, the H pawn is simply going to be able to run freely because this bishop is of the wrong color and not going to be able to stop it from moving. White will win the game.
